The core REST module (`openmrs-module-webservices.rest`) calls `ProgramWorkflowService.savePatientProgram` from three resource classes. The two programenrollment subclasses inherit the enrollment save path, so they are affected too.

1. **`ProgramEnrollmentResource1_8.save`** calls it directly to persist a `PatientProgram` (enrollment). This is the `/programenrollment` resource's create/update path.
2. **`PatientStateResource1_8.save`** adds a state to the parent enrollment and calls the service to save it. Its `delete` also calls the service after voiding the last state. This is the `/programenrollment/{uuid}/state` sub-resource.
3. **`PatientProgramAttributeResource2_2`** calls the service from both `save` and `delete` (soft-delete sets voided and then saves the parent enrollment). This is the enrollment attribute sub-resource.

Inherited paths: `ProgramEnrollmentResource1_10` extends 1_8 without overriding `save`, and `ProgramEnrollmentResource2_2` extends 1_10. Both therefore route through `ProgramEnrollmentResource1_8.save`.

I did not check the `openmrs1_9` or other resource packages beyond the grep hits, and the grep matched only these three REST classes. Outside the REST module, `PatientServiceImpl` in openmrs-core also calls the service, but that is not part of `/ws/rest/v1`.
